svg.text: B — Workflows vs. skills
The distinction that governs everything else: who owns the file, and what is allowed to change it.
SKILLS — plugin-owned machinery
Shipped identical to every user. Never user-refinable.
Changed only by a plugin update.
setup-openaos
Scaffolds the foundation once, then hands off to the builder.
build-workflow
One engine, two modes: instantiate a use case, or design-new.
refine-workflow
The one sanctioned way a definition file changes in place.
Properties
· Live in the plugin, not the workspace
· Identical for every user — no local variation
· Uninstalling removes them and leaves the workspace intact
· Not covered by the drift invariant — not the user's files
To change one
Edit the design spec → §36.1 readiness review →
§36.2 regenerate the plugin → users update. See diagram G.
WORKFLOWS — user-owned artifacts
Scaffolded into the workspace and tailored by interview.
Refinable. Covered by the drift invariant.
Use-case workflows — five predefined
inbox triage · research assistant · writing assistant
learning assistant · organizer / declutter — plus design-new
Governance workflows — five, always installed
daily-startup · end-of-day · weekly-review
monthly-review · feedback
Properties
· Live in the user's /workflows folder
· Every one is interview-authored — nothing generic scaffolded
· Zero use-case workflows after setup is a valid state
· A workflow run never edits a definition file as a side effect
· Governance ones may be revised, never removed (§16.1)
To change one
Run refine-workflow → interview → diff preview → Proceed.
Or a plugin update, also gated. See diagram D.
Skills author and refine workflows — never the reverse
If you remember one thing: a skill is code we ship, a workflow is a document the user owns.
Fixing a skill means regenerating the plugin; fixing a workflow means an interview.
